unit: Spring 2: Understanding the Qur'an and teaching
source: Written for quran/y11 lesson 6 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Reading translations and tafsir wisely rule card and examples)
intro: Lesson 6. Read the rule and say every example aloud. Point to each word in your mushaf. Then answer the questions.

panels.title: What a translation can do
points: Gives the meaning in another language
Only the Arabic is the Qur'an

head: Not this
This
rows: Quoting 'Do not approach prayer' (4:43) on its own
The ayah continues: 'while you are intoxicated until you know what you are saying'

questions.q: Read 18:6 in Arabic and two English renderings on the slide. What shade of meaning differs, and what stays the same?
questions.a: Both convey the Prophet's ﷺ grief over people's disbelief; wording ('kill yourself through grief' or 'grieve yourself to death') differs in strength.

questions.q: Source check (Forms long answer): a post quotes part of an ayah to make a claim. Explain three steps you would take before accepting it. Today's rota group recites Ya-Sin 36:1 to 24.
questions.a: Check the full ayah in Arabic; read its context; read a reliable tafsir or ask a teacher.

questions.q: Extend: name two reliable classical tafsir works.
questions.a: For example: Tafsir at-Tabari and Tafsir Ibn Kathir.

questions.q: The safest way to understand a difficult ayah is ...
options: read its context and a reliable tafsir, and ask a teacher
questions.a: A) read its context and a reliable tafsir, and ask a teacher. Context, reliable tafsir and asking those with knowledge.

questions.q: Think again: Online, people often post a single line of the Qur'an to prove a point. What could go wrong?
questions.a: It may be cut from its context or mistranslated, giving a meaning the ayah does not have.
